Four project types · Four perspectives · Git for scholarly editing

Workflow models

Read the diagram as text
  1. Git and XML tools: Edit TEI → Check + commit → Git data version → XML queries → Publication. Git holds the authoritative collection. Editors compare and check changes, record them as commits and transfer them to the shared repository. XML tools read the files. Publication can be generated statically; a running application is also possible.
  2. Git leads; the database provides access: Git data version → Checked import → XML database → Query / interface → Feedback. Git holds the authoritative edition data. A checked import builds the database collection. The database serves queries and the interface. Editorial corrections return to Git through the agreed review process; the database is then updated. There is no uncontrolled second place for edits.
  3. Edit in a database and connect it to Git: Edit in database → Defined export → Compare + check → Git commit → Release. An existing database interface remains the authoritative editing environment. A defined export passes checked changes to Git, which versions the exported data and associated programs. Editing exported files and the database simultaneously requires an agreed reconciliation process.

Editorial basis: the two supplied working documents on Git and XML databases. Text, translation, schematic diagrams and implementation were created with AI assistance. Version 1.0 · 28 October 2026. Diagrams show workflow models, not an actual installation.
